name: Łódź Voivodeship
summary_text: Łódzkie was one of the five voivodeships that formally adopted an "anti-LGBT ideology" resolution by mid-2020, placing approximately one-third of Poland's territory under declarations whose stated purpose was to exclude LGBTQ public events. It sits in the PiS-vote heartland belt running east of the Łódź metro area. The resolution was struck down or repealed in the 2021 wave following EU Commission funding threats. No march ban, coordinated attack, or county-level holdout comparable to Subcarpathian's Łańcut (2025) or Podlaskie's Białystok County is documented for Łódzkie. The sub-national finding is the regional resolution itself and its location in the eastern conservative bloc; the practical visitor-facing exposure is the general social climate of that bloc rather than a specific enforcement or violence event. Score of 0.48 sits 0.04 below the national 0.52, matching Małopolska (0.48) for having a voivodeship-level resolution without an additional capital-city positive counterweight or a documented enforcement/violence episode. Well above Subcarpathian (0.42) and Podlaskie (0.44), both of which carry specific ban or assault evidence.

sources.claim_summary: Encyclopedia overview of Poland's 'LGBT-free zones': by June 2020 some 100 municipalities and five voivodeships - Lodzkie among them - had adopted resolutions covering about a third of the country; mostly lobbied by the ultra-conservative Ordo Iuris institute, legally meaningless but stigmatising; by 6 February 2024 a Warsaw administrative court repealed the last such declaration and by 24 April 2025 all had been withdrawn or invalidated.

sources.title: Poland’s LGBT-Free Zones: From Declaration to Repeal - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: Legal-overview article on the rise and fall of Poland's LGBT-free zones: between 2019 and 2025 more than 100 local governments adopted 'LGBT ideology'-free resolutions or Ordo Iuris-drafted family-rights charters covering roughly a third of the country at peak; the documents created no criminal penalties but symbolically sidelined LGBT residents from civic life; the national human-rights commissioner's litigation led courts to strike them down as unconstitutional, the EU threatened to freeze billions in regional funds, and the last remaining zone was abolished in spring 2025.
